newsitem.title: UK: North Sea steady, cash Brent spreads rise modestly.
newsitem.headline: North Sea steady, cash Brent spreads rise modestly.

text.p: Cash Brent spreads and North Sea differentials were stable to modestly higher on Thursday in line with outright market gains spurred by a lengthy spell of cold weather across Europe.
February Brent, up 50 cents at $24.30 a barrel, pulled bids on the Feb/Mar spread to +60 cents but both paper and physical trade was slim.
Dated Brent for mid-January was looking a shade firmer at about Jan +15 cents but remained hostage to opposing factions looking to influence related swaps trade.
CFDs were marginally firmer in line with the higher Brent numbers, taking next week to Feb +15-22 cents.
Dealers said the cancellation by Shell on Monday of a a Brent cargo due to load Jan 15-17 had helped underpin differentials.
Improved refining margins based on strong heating oil demand also were a positive factor for North Sea differentials, they said.
Gullfaks C for Jan 24-26 traded at Dated Brent plus 44 cents, unchanged from the grade's last trade 10 days ago.
Nevertheless, both sets of Thursday's Brent dates were five o'clocked leaving Mobil and Phibro with unwanted Jan 17-19 loaders.
In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals was valued unchanged at about a $1.15 discount to Dated Brent despite better margins.
Dealers said a cargo on the water was preventing prices rising.
"People are looking at Iraqi arrivals and taking stock before they agree to buy at higher numbers," said a dealer.
